claims.text: The US Geological Survey's event page for us7000tbwb (GeoJSON feed) records a magnitude 5.2 event at 2026-08-26T02:52:10 UTC, 55 km NW of Kodārī, Nepal (28.271°N, 85.515°E), with type 'landslide' and status 'reviewed' -- titled 'M 5.2 Landslide - 55 km NW of Kodārī, Nepal.' USGS initially detected the signal as a magnitude 4.4 seismic event but, after analysis of long-period seismic waves and satellite imagery, determined it was a glacial collapse and debris flow rather than a tectonic earthquake.

GDACS's earthquake-channel report for the reclassified event (26 August 2026, 02:52 UTC, 28.271°N 85.515°E, depth 5 km) records an overall Green alert with a GDACS score of 0 across all impact metrics and about 6,000 people exposed to MMI V (moderate) or greater shaking. A separate media-headlines module on the same report page cites third-party news reports of more than 1,300 people missing and approximately 180 deaths in the Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse disaster, which are explicitly not GDACS's own assessed figures.

UN News, 'Deadly floods cause widespread destruction in China, Nepal' (26 August 2026): flooding 'has claimed many lives, left people missing and caused widespread destruction'; Nepalese authorities report some 10,000 households are in need of immediate relief. WFP is providing emergency rations and logistics support; WHO has deployed two staff with medical kits sufficient for about 10,000 people for three months plus tents and logistics; UNICEF is deploying staff and relief-supply trucks; UNDP is mobilizing data-management support and UN Volunteers; Save the Children is deploying staff to Nuwakot district; and the Nepalese Red Cross has dispatched 200 emergency shelter packages.

UN News, 'Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster' (27 August 2026): in China, 'around 560 people remain missing, according to the authorities.' UN relief chief Tom Fletcher said an initial $2 million has been released from the UN's Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) 'to save lives with emergency medical care, shelter, water'; WHO has dispatched an interagency emergency health kit sufficient for basic health services for up to 10,000 people plus six multipurpose tents; UNICEF says at least 17,000 children have been impacted and is 'scaling up support,' adding it 'urgently need[s] more resources to reach every child in need.'

GDACS's earthquake-channel report page for this event (eventid 1561857), checked 28 August 2026, continues to show an overall Green alert (GDACS score 0) with about 6,000 people exposed to MMI≥V shaking, unchanged from the 26 August assessment. Its media-headlines module now displays a news report headlined 'Nepal: 475 bodies recovered as Bhotekoshi flood death toll rises, rescuers...' (dated 28 August 2026, 8:57am), alongside a headline that Nepal has ordered rescuers to safety amid new flood risks from glacial-lake overflow; these remain third-party media figures relayed on the GDACS page, not GDACS's own assessed casualty count.

description: A glacial collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border triggered a catastrophic flash flood down the Bhotekoshi/Trishuli river system through Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, Nepal, on the morning of 26 August 2026. USGS classifies the triggering event as a magnitude-5.2-equivalent landslide rather than a tectonic earthquake, and GDACS's own earthquake-channel assessment remains Green with about 6,000 people exposed to strong shaking near the source. No authoritative body has yet published its own confirmed death toll: UN agencies report roughly 10,000 households in Nepal are in need of immediate relief, at least 17,000 children have been affected, about 560 people remain missing in China, and an initial $2 million has been released from the UN's Central Emergency Response Fund for emergency medical care, shelter and water, while a news headline relayed on GDACS's report page on 28 August cites 475 bodies recovered -- a third-party figure not yet confirmed by an authoritative source. Search-and-rescue operations continue along the affected river corridor, and several hydropower stations in the area have been damaged.

impact.summary: No authoritative source has yet published its own confirmed death toll for the 26 August glacial-collapse flash flood. UN agencies report about 10,000 households in Nepal need immediate relief, at least 17,000 children have been affected, roughly 560 people remain missing in China, and the UN's Central Emergency Response Fund has released an initial $2 million for emergency medical care, shelter and water. A news headline relayed on GDACS's earthquake-channel report page (Green alert, about 6,000 people exposed to MMI V or greater shaking) cited 475 bodies recovered as of 28 August, but this remains an unconfirmed third-party figure rather than an official tally.

location.region: Rasuwa & Nuwakot Districts, Nepal; Gyirong County, Tibet, China

event.scale: USGS M5.2-equivalent glacial collapse/landslide (reclassified from a tectonic earthquake); GDACS Green

name: Glacial Collapse Flash Flood — Rasuwa, Nepal & Tibet, China

updates.text: UN agencies scaled up their response as the toll grew: about 10,000 households in Nepal need immediate relief, 17,000+ children are affected, ~560 remain missing in China, and CERF released an initial $2 million for emergency medical care, shelter and water. A GDACS-relayed headline on 28 August cites 475 bodies recovered, an unconfirmed third-party figure.
